title: Washington Post 'Lucky to be alive' article on people who skipped work on 9/11
summary: Rupert Sheldrake tells of Washington Post 'Lucky to be alive' article on people who skipped work on 9/11, about 2001 at New York, and reports it citing named sources. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: there was an article called lucky to be alive in the Washington Post that actually told the stories of people who hadn't gone to work that day

plain: A British biologist, Rupert Sheldrake, points to a Washington Post article called "Lucky to be alive" about the 9/11 attacks of 2001 on New York. He says it told the stories of people who did not go to work that day, which he offers as a sign that some people may sense danger before it happens.
